title: Prospective Study on Factors influencing Lymph Node Yield in Neck Dissection of Head and Neck Tumours
summary:
The patient was diagnosed with cancer in the head and neck area. A common treatment is the surgical removal of tumours and lymph nodes in the neck area (neck dissection). If the primary tumour (the original cancerous growth from which metastases spread) is operable, targeted removal of the neck lymph nodes is recommended in addition to its removal. Both confirmed and potential metastases in the lymph nodes should be removed to prevent further spread of the tumour. Clinically inconspicuous lymph nodes that may contain malignant cells are also removed. 

The current standard of care is the targeted removal of certain lymphatic regions. The lymph node regions of the neck are divided into levels (levels I to VI). Depending on the location and type of tumour, certain lymph node levels are susceptible to lymph node metastases, e.g. levels I-III in oral cavity tumours. Unaffected levels and structures are spared, which improves the restoration of normal bodily functions after surgery.

Studies have shown that the number of lymph nodes removed during surgical treatment depends on several factors. These include the patient's age, body weight, height, tumour stage, tumour location and previous radiotherapy.

It is currently unclear which factors influence the lymph node yield of neck lymph node dissection in head and neck tumours. The number could depend on the surgeon's experience, the respective lymph node regions removed, the type of neck lymph node dissection, and tumour- and patient-related factors, among other things. The aim of this study is to determine these parameters more precisely and to find out which factors influence lymph node yield.
conditions: Cancer in the head and neck area

interventions.name: This study investigates possible factors that influence lymph node yield during neck lymph node dissection in head and neck tumours. The study is a surgical study in which additional data is collected during standard treatment. All participants in the study undergo surgery under the same conditions,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Head and neck tumour diagnosis
-Capacity to give consent
Exclusion criteria:
-Patient age < 18
-Patient has no head and neck tumour diagnosis
-Patient is not capable of giving consent
